plan: dispatch://SMOKE-2/artifact/plan-md (plan.md v1) is the full plan; this file records the required skills, the two plan checks, and the departures from the spec.

implement: skill://legion-worker: the implementer pushes code without a skip-checks trailer, opens the pull request with the line 'Dispatch: SMOKE-2', writes .legion/SMOKE-2/implement.json with a proof array, and runs the post-merge production check.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: it defines the pull-request body template, what a proof is (surface, command, observed, head SHA, negative control), and that a docs-only diff runs no ce-simplify-code pass and omits the Thermo line, which is exactly this diff.

skill://legion-retro: the same agent is revived for retro, whose docs/solutions/<category>/<slug>-SMOKE-2.md naming and final .legion/SMOKE-2/ removal commit are what acceptance criterion 3 is read against.
skill://dispatch: retro's Dispatch message and the production-check message on SMOKE-2 are written through the dispatch command, never a GitHub issue comment.

none (repository skills): the repository has no AGENTS.md, no pull-request template, no skills directory and nothing under .github/ beyond workflows/, so it contributes no skill of its own and retro's body-derivation steps 2-4 are skipped.
test: skill://legion-worker: the tester verifies the implementer's proof, records implementerProof, failures and its own proof in .legion/SMOKE-2/test.json, and completes with a verdict.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: it says the tester drives the application rather than re-running CI, reads CI for everything static, and that a predecessor handoff carrying no proof is a test failure rather than a gap the tester fills.

none (repository skills): the repository has no AGENTS.md and no test suite (.github/workflows/ci.yml job check is 'sleep 20 && exit 0'), so no repository testing convention exists and no red test is written for a one-file Markdown diff.
review: skill://legion-worker: the reviewer writes the body's 'Look at first' and 'Not proven / risk' lines and records verdict, counts and keyFindings in .legion/SMOKE-2/review.json.
skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: it fixes the order of a review round and the approval of the head that retro and the merger build on.

skill://legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: threads, including any the operator's fixture App opens on this branch, are answered and resolved one by one, and the reviewer names the bot threads it accepts rather than resolving them.
none (repository skills): the repository has no AGENTS.md, no CODEOWNERS and no review checklist, so it imposes no review convention beyond the required gate check.

findings.finding: F1: all three acceptance criteria are post-merge facts, but Legion requires the implementer to prove the change before its phase completes; nothing said which half is proven where.
findings.answer: plan.md section 3 splits every criterion into a pre-merge half with its surface and command at the implementer's code head, an explicit 'Not proven / risk' bullet naming the post-merge remainder, and a post-merge command the implementer's production check runs at the merge commit.

findings.finding: F2: criterion 2's 'merged head' names either the pull-request head the ruleset gates or the squash commit on main, read by different commands.
findings.answer: plan.md section 3 C2 proves both: check-runs for the name 'gate' at the pull-request head, and at the merge commit both the check-runs read and 'gh run list --commit <M>' for the push-event fail-on-demand run. It also pins the required-set read (ruleset 24471196 answers 'gate'; branch protection answers 403 to our App, recorded rather than worked around). Both forms were calibrated on the prior run's merge commit bc2c34c2.

findings.finding: F3: criterion 1's mergedBy is not under Legion's control (the two prior comparable runs were merged by the fixture App), and the login literal differs between gh pr view and the REST API.
findings.answer: Measured: 'gh api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/582 --jq .user.login,.merged_by.login' prints trajectory-s-legion-implementer[bot] for both, while 'gh pr view 582 --json author,mergedBy' prints app/trajectory-s-legion-implementer with no [bot]. plan.md pins the REST form and the [bot] literal and records that the architect's steer named a command that prints the other string. The risk that an outside actor merges first is in plan.md section 5 and is raised to the architect, whose decision it is; the plan proceeds on the daemon-submitted path.

findings.finding: F4: criterion 3's 'nothing else' is threatened by a foreign .fail-me fixture push onto the issue branch (precedent on pull request 571) and by the untracked .codegraph/.gitignore in the workspace.
findings.answer: plan.md section 3 C3 adds a path guard every phase runs before each push (jj diff --from main@origin --to @- --name-only must list only smoke/SMOKE-2.md, .legion/SMOKE-2/ and docs/solutions/*-SMOKE-2.md), and section 4 names the forward-only recovery for a foreign commit. .codegraph/ was measured not to be a risk: the file is untracked and 'jj status' reports the working copy has no changes.

findings.finding: F5: criterion 3's predicate is not precise enough to check, and a retro that writes no learning document could leave the merged head with no CI.
findings.answer: plan.md section 3 C3 states the predicate as a command: every path in the merge commit's file list matches ^smoke/SMOKE-2\.md$ or ^docs/solutions/.+-SMOKE-2\.md$ with the marker present, plus a 404 for the .legion/SMOKE-2 contents read. The zero-document case is explicitly allowed because skill://legion-retro permits it, and the no-CI worry does not arise: retro's push carries the .legion removal and so is a code push with no skip-checks trailer, which starts the gate workflow.

findings.finding: F6: 'the date', the file's text and 'every phase' are not checkable as written.
findings.answer: plan.md section 1 pins the file's exact 208 bytes as a printf reference every phase cmp's against, with wc -c, wc -l, trailing-byte and ASCII assertions; it fixes the date as the run date 2026-10-16 and the Dispatch project string as SMOKE (dispatch projects), not the daemon's project token 'smoke'; and it states that the gVisor sentence is the issue author's attestation, so the machine check is byte presence, not truth.

findings.finding: F7: 'the first issue a Legion daemon on GKE Autopilot took from Dispatch to a merged pull request' and 'every phase ran in an Agent Sandbox pod under gVisor' are claims no command in this repository can settle.
findings.answer: plan.md sections 1 and 5 record both as attestations of the issue's author, name what is checked (byte presence) and what is not (their truth), and note the only corroboration available (this pod's /proc/version reads 'Linux version 4.19.0-gvisor'). No phase is asked to prove them and no phase may weaken the file to avoid them.

findings.finding: F8: each check needs a negative control that would actually have failed, and the obvious one for the gate check would cost a red CI round.
findings.answer: plan.md section 3 names one per check: for the file content, the same read at the base SHA returning 404 and a one-byte-altered reference failing cmp; for the gate, the existing red run 38794798972 at 20634d1dc539504314a2cbe34d86c10986d10e99, cited and never recreated by pushing .fail-me; for the .legion absence, the same contents read at the reviewer-approved head returning 200, which is why READY records that SHA; for the identity check, pull request 575 whose merged_by is the fixture App.

findings.finding: F9: four repository-specific facts (no derived pull-request body content, docs-only diff so no simplify pass or Thermo line, no test suite so no red test, and criterion 1 must be read at a named SHA rather than a bare main ref) would each cost a round if a phase had to discover them.
findings.answer: plan.md section 4 states all four as per-phase instructions, and section 3 C1's post-merge read pins the merge SHA and proves it is on main with 'gh api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/compare/<M>...main --jq .status' at a recorded time, never a bare ?ref=main read.
